q-pt-two.standard: Multiply each partner's capital by his months. Write the ratio, add the parts, take his part ÷ total × profit. For 'find total profit', divide the known share by his fraction.
q-pt-two.fast: Cancel common factors before multiplying: 90,000×8 : 1,50,000×5 → 9×8 : 15×5 = 72 : 75 = 24 : 25. Drop zeros and common factors first, then work with the small numbers.
q-pt-two.ultra: Profit ÷ (sum of parts) first, then multiply by his part: 50,000 ÷ 49 ≈ 1,020 → ×25 ≈ 25,510. If the given share divides exactly by his ratio part (18,900 ÷ 7 = 2,700) your ratio is almost certainly right.
q-pt-two.eliminate: (1) Compare the capital-months roughly: 7,20,000 against 7,50,000 are close, so Q gets just over half of 50,000 (about 25,000 to 26,000). Only ₹25,510 is that close; ₹32,000 and ₹35,000 are far too big. (2) When the numbers are nice, a share is a whole multiple of profit ÷ sum of parts: 60,000 ÷ 5 = 12,000, so only ₹24,000 can be P's share.
traps: Ignoring time and splitting by capital alone.
Giving the answer for the wrong partner (read who the question asks for).
In 'find total profit', multiplying by the wrong fraction (use his part, not the other partner's).

q-pt-late.standard: Find each partner's months in the business (12 − months before joining). Multiply capital × months, make the ratio, then share the profit.
q-pt-late.fast: Put the capitals in thousands and divide the capital-months by a common factor: 1,200 : 1,050 : 1,000 → ÷50 → 24 : 21 : 20. Tushar = 20 of 65 parts = 4/13.
q-pt-late.ultra: Reduce the final fraction before multiplying: 20/65 = 4/13, then 1,50,000 ÷ 13 ≈ 11,538 → ×4 = 46,154. Use 1/13 ≈ 0.0769 as a quick check.
q-pt-late.eliminate: (1) Tushar has the smallest capital-months (1,000 against 1,200 and 1,050), so his share is under one third of 1,50,000, which is ₹50,000. That drops ₹55,000. (2) The three are nearly equal, so he gets about 30%, around ₹45,000. That drops ₹35,500. (3) Between ₹46,154 and ₹45,250: the fraction 4/13 does not divide 1,50,000 evenly, so the exact answer is not a round number, which points to ₹46,154.
traps: Counting months before joining instead of months after (joined at month 5 → he stays 7 months, not 5).
Forgetting that the founder stays all 12 months.

q-pt-working.standard: Take the working partner's % off the profit first. Share the balance in the investment ratio. His total = commission + his share of the balance.
q-pt-working.fast: Total fraction = c% + (1 − c%) × his ratio part. For 15% and 2 : 7 → 0.15 + 0.85 × 2/9 = 0.3389. Then × profit.
q-pt-working.ultra: Choose the split that divides cleanly: 81,000 is a multiple of 9, so 2/9 of the balance is easy. 68,850 ÷ 9 = 7,650 → ×2 = 15,300; add 12,150 → 27,450.
q-pt-working.eliminate: Squeeze 2/9 between 1/5 and 1/4. Then M's total is between 15% + 0.85 × 20% = 32% of the profit (₹25,920) and 15% + 0.85 × 25% = 36.25% (₹29,363). Only ₹27,450 fits; ₹24,000, ₹30,000 and ₹33,000 are all outside.
traps: Taking his ratio share of the full profit and then adding the commission (double counting).
Taking the commission as a % of his own share instead of the whole profit.
Forgetting to add the commission to his total.

q-pt-pasture.standard: Pick one animal as the standard. Convert every other animal using the given equivalence. Multiply animals × months for each person, then split the rent in that ratio.
q-pt-pasture.fast: Pick the unit so that every equivalent becomes a whole number. 2 oxen = 5 goats and 3 goats = 4 sheep → in 'thirds of a sheep': ox = 10, goat = 4, sheep = 3. Then no fractions appear anywhere.
q-pt-pasture.ultra: After converting, cancel the common factor of the two totals: 1,140 : 1,212 → ÷12 → 95 : 101. Fraction = 95/196. Check the direction first: 3 cows = 7 goats means 1 cow = 7/3 goat, not the other way round.
q-pt-pasture.eliminate: Estimate the fraction: X's total ≈ 285, Y's ≈ 303, so X ≈ 285/588 ≈ 0.485, a little under half. Any option above ½ or far below it is out. This leaves 90/196 (0.459) and 95/196 (0.485), and one rough division settles it.
traps: Reading the equivalence upside down (cow worth 3/7 goat instead of 7/3).
Leaving one animal type out of a person's total.
